comment: Intentional React↔Android divergences for visual testing (task #370/#373, artin 2026-07-06). Each entry documents a KNOWN, ACCEPTED difference so triage sweeps do not re-report it as a bug. direction values: 'react-adopts-later' = the android behavior is the desired product feature and React should eventually catch up (do NOT change android; react work is deferred); 'platform-difference' = both sides are correct for their platform, never align. Optional appliesTo key (spec: provider-pair-first PR-3, task #430) scopes an entry to a pair class: 'baselineOnly' (react__<platform> pairs), 'crossPlatform' (mobile↔mobile pairs like android__ios), 'allPairs'. When appliesTo is absent it defaults by direction: react-adopts-later → baselineOnly (it describes distance from the react reference), platform-difference → allPairs. Update this file in the same PR whenever the owner declares a new intentional divergence or retires one.

divergences.note: Android shows a per-task timestamp at the card's top-right (relative format). React's panel currently shows none — react should adopt it. Declared by artin 2026-07-06 (task #373 thread).
Android shows the assignee (Unassigned/@name) at the card's bottom-left. React should adopt it; do not remove from android.

divergences.area: filter row presence and wrap layout
divergences.note: The filter chip row (Channel/Creator/Assignee) is an android feature; its single-row layout vs react's wrapped layout is a platform difference and must not be 'fixed'. Chip casing and visual styling DO align to react (Title case, shared chip tokens).
Deliberately skipped; artin deprioritized this case (task #342 era).

React says 'Sign out of this browser' (web-appropriate); Android says 'Sign out on this device' (mobile-appropriate) in both the log-out subtitle and the confirm message. Both are correct for their platform — never align. Landed in android via task #381 (PR #147). Everything else in this case aligns.

divergences.area: bare #number task chips in message bodies
divergences.note: Android tags every bare #number as a task chip regardless of whether the ref resolves; react gates task refs on known/loaded entities (MessageItem.tsx known-set checks), so unknown refs like '#520' render as plain text on react but as task chips on android. artin ruled keep android's tag-everything behavior ('就全部 tag 呗，反正点了之后会报错没有的', 2026-07-07, task #416 closed). Mention styling is no longer an accepted divergence: self mentions use yellow chips, known other mentions use bold black underline, and unknown mentions remain plain text on both platforms.

divergences.area: filter chip row (count, sort chip, wrap)
divergences.note: React shows more filter chips (incl. a sort/Recent chip) wrapped across two rows; android's search filter row is a single non-wrapping row with fewer chips. This is an intentional mobile layout — a platform difference, not a defect (mirrors the tasks.panel filter-row declaration). Chip casing/styling still align.

Android uses a single combined Forward modal with an inline destination list; react uses a two-step flow (search targets, then a separate preview/compose step). Both are correct for their platform — a mobile UX adaptation, never align.

divergences.area: vertical content overflow within the fixed canvas
divergences.note: The skeleton fixture is deliberately matched to react's fixed 150px canvas; the content stack overflowing into the bottom padding mirrors CSS (documented in UiSkeletonVisualContent). The residual is a sub-pixel overflow detail, intentional — not a defect.

divergences.area: account section header label (Profile vs ACCOUNT)
divergences.note: Android labels the account settings section 'Profile'; react labels it 'ACCOUNT'. A platform naming choice, not a defect. (Localization of the android label is handled under the Account i18n task; the cross-platform label difference itself is intentional.)

Android keeps ALL-CAPS tab labels (deliberate mobile brand style) while web MobileTabBar renders Title Case; the smoke fixture's selected tab also differs from web's route-derived active tab. Not a drift to converge.

divergences.area: activity card timestamp placement (right-aligned tag row vs title row)
divergences.note: Android puts the relative timestamp on the top (channel-tag) row, right-aligned to the card's right edge; react puts it beside the title, which artin ruled steals width from the real message content (#wg-nightly-visual-fix 2026-07-17, re mobile#1039 and #1171). Android is the desired behavior — react should move its timestamp to the right-aligned tag row. The title and the rows below do not move. Do NOT change android.

divergences.area: GitHub social button color (black vs white)
divergences.note: Android renders Continue with GitHub as a black button; react's SocialProviderButton is bg-white for every provider. artin ruled the android black button is correct ('github 按钮不需要换，我觉得我们的对的', #wg-nightly-visual-fix 2026-07-17, re mobile#962). Do NOT change android; whether react adopts black is a web-lane decision.

divergences.area: channel/mention refs inside Markdown link labels
divergences.note: Web renders channel/mention refs inside a Markdown link label as chips (splitting the link visually); Android's Raft dialect keeps the whole label inside one external link. artin ruled 2026-07-25 (#proj-visual-testing:58e605e1) that Web stays as-is — do not re-report this case's label-chip delta as a bug. Task refs in labels already match (both keep the link).
